title: Openness and ind-etale invariance of a labelled regular-coordinate locus
statement: Let $S$ be a quasi-excellent Noetherian scheme [def-exc-excellent-ring, def-pc-scheme], let $X\to S$ be of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $C_1,\ldots,C_m,D\hookrightarrow X$ be closed subschemes [def-weil-closed-immersion] with ideals $I_1,\ldots,I_m,K$. Define $G\subseteq X$ as follows. A point $x$ belongs to $G$ if $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme] and, after discarding the indices $j$ with $(I_j)_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, the remaining ideals are $(t_1),\ldots,(t_r)$ for distinct members of one regular system of parameters of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters], and $K_x=(t_1\cdots t_r)$. The empty product is $1$. Then $G$ is open. On $G$, the $C_j$ are regular effective Cartier divisors where nonempty, their scheme-theoretic intersections are regular of local codimension equal to the number of intersecting distinct labels, and $D$ is their reduced scheme-theoretic union [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal, def-pc-fibre-product]. Every regular Noetherian scheme with a strict normal crossings boundary, labelled by its reduced irreducible components [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], satisfies this coordinate condition everywhere. If $g:Y\to X$ is an affine locally ind-etale morphism with $Y$ Noetherian, meaning that its maps on affine coordinate rings are filtered colimits of etale algebras [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], then the coordinate locus for the pulled-back labelled closed subschemes is exactly $g^{-1}(G)$. These assertions do not require the individual $C_j$ to be globally integral.

source.place: Tag 0BI9 (definition-strict-normal-crossings) and Tag 0BIA (lemma-strict-normal-crossings), including its local-equation proof; openness uses more-algebra.tex Tag 07P7 (definition-J) for all marked intersections and openness of the finite-presentation Cartier/regular-sequence conditions. Ind-etale invariance is the Noetherian filtered-etale version of more-algebra.tex Tags 07QP (lemma-dimension-etale-extension) and 0AH0 (lemma-regular-etale-extension): the flat local maps have field closed fibre, preserve dimension and identify cotangent spaces after residue-field extension. This is a general interface extracted from these arguments, not a claim that 0BIA states the whole interface verbatim.

proof.text: Work locally at $x\in G$ in an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$, with $x$ corresponding to $\mathfrak p$. Since $S$ has a finite affine cover and finite type includes quasi-compactness [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], the inverse images of that cover form a finite quasi-compact cover of $X$, so $X$ is quasi-compact. By [lem-per-quasi-excellent-finite-type-stability], $X$ is Noetherian and $R$ is quasi-excellent. Thus $R$ and every finite type $R$-algebra have open regular locus, by the J-2 clause of [def-exc-excellent-ring]. In particular this applies to each quotient of $R$ by a finitely generated ideal. Use [lem-sfb-closed-component-stalk-calculus] to identify all the given stalk ideals with localized ideals of $R$ and all closed-intersection local rings with quotients.

source.place: Tag 07P7 (definition-J), applied to affine rings and their finite type quotients

proof.text: Renumber the labels through $x$ as $1,\ldots,r$. Choose $a_j\in I_j$ whose germ is a unit multiple of the prescribed parameter $t_j$: a fraction representing $t_j\in I_jR_{\mathfrak p}$ has numerator in $I_j$ and denominator outside $\mathfrak p$. Multiplying individual parameters by units preserves the ideal generated by the full list and its length, so gives another regular system of parameters. Shrink $U$ to arrange simultaneously $I_j=(a_j)$ for $j\le r$, $I_j=R$ for all other labels, and $K=(a_1\cdots a_r)$. Here is the finite clearing argument: every ideal of $R$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] applied to $R$. For each generator, equality of the two localized ideals gives an ideal membership after multiplying by one denominator outside $\mathfrak p$, by [lem-exc-localization-ideal-membership-clearing]. Invert the product of these finitely many denominators, in both directions for the equality involving $K$. All the equalities then hold on that principal neighborhood. The argument includes $r=0$, when the required equality is $K=R$.

source.place: Tag 0BIA (lemma-strict-normal-crossings), local equations; finite localization argument written out from algebra.tex localization definitions

proof.text: For each $H\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ put $J_H=(a_j:j\in H)$. By [lem-sfb-transverse-prime-ideal-parameters](b), $(R/J_H)_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular, including $H=\varnothing$. The preceding J-2 observation shows that the nonregular locus in $\operatorname{Spec}(R/J_H)=V(J_H)$ is closed there, hence closed in $U$, and it avoids $x$. Remove all these finitely many closed sets. After taking a smaller affine principal neighborhood, the ambient local ring at every point is regular, and for every $H$ and every point $q\in V(J_H)$ its quotient by the germs $a_j$, $j\in H$, is regular. This uses the regular locus of each closed intersection in that closed intersection, rather than an assertion that a closed intersection is an open subscheme of $U$.

For each subset $H$, order its elements increasingly. At $x$ the corresponding tuple $a_H$ is an initial segment of a permutation of a full regular system of parameters. It is therefore a regular sequence by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence]. By [lem-exc-regular-sequence-principal-neighbourhood] and a common shrinking over the finitely many $H$, these tuples are regular sequences on the affine neighborhood. At a point $q$, let $H(q)=\{j:a_j\in\mathfrak q\}$ and $A=R_{\mathfrak q}$. Weak regularity localizes by [lem-exc-weakly-regular-sequence-localization]. For $H=H(q)$ the final quotient is nonzero since every selected germ lies in the maximal ideal, so the localized tuple is a regular sequence. Consequently [lem-trf-regular-sequence-dimension-formula] gives $\dim A/(a_j:j\in H(q))=\dim A-|H(q)|$. The empty tuple gives $A/(0)=A$.

source.place: Tags 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM) and 061L (lemma-regular-sequence-in-neighbourhood); regular-sequence dimension formula is the statement of lem-trf-regular-sequence-dimension-formula

proof.text: Write $H=H(q)$, $s=|H|$, $J=(a_j:j\in H)A$, $d=\dim A$, and $k=A/\mathfrak m$. Both $A$ and $A/J$ are regular by Step 3. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension], their cotangent dimensions are $d$ and $d-s$. The quotient map $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\to\mathfrak m/(J+\mathfrak m^2)$ is surjective with kernel $(J+\mathfrak m^2)/\mathfrak m^2$, so that kernel has dimension $s$. The $s$ classes of the displayed generators $a_j$ span it and are therefore a basis. Extend them to a basis of $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ and lift the additional basis vectors to $\mathfrak m$. The ideal $\mathfrak m$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite]. Nakayama [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators], applied to this module, says that the resulting $d$ elements generate $\mathfrak m$. They are a regular system of parameters by [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. The other $a_j$ are units at $q$, and Step 2 gives $K_q=(\prod_{j\in H}a_j)$, since the discarded factors are units. Thus every point of this neighborhood is in $G$, proving openness.

source.place: Tag 00NR (lemma-regular-quotient-regular), cotangent-space calculation in its proof; Nakayama and the definition of a regular system of parameters

proof.text: On the now open scheme $G$, apply [lem-sfb-transverse-prime-ideal-parameters](b) at each point. It says that every active coordinate equation is a nonzerodivisor, its quotient is regular, and the quotient by any subset of $s$ active coordinates is regular of dimension $\dim\mathcal O_{G,x}-s$. At a point off a given label its ideal is the unit ideal. By [lem-sfb-stalk-nonzerodivisor-cartier-spreading] these stalk ideals define effective Cartier divisors, allowing empty ones. The stalk descriptions of [lem-sfb-closed-component-stalk-calculus] identify the stated quotients with the intersections of the labelled closed subschemes, so give precisely their regularity and local codimension assertion. The same parameter-product lemma gives $(\prod t_j)=\bigcap(t_j)$, a radical ideal, at each stalk. Thus $D|_G$ is reduced and equals the reduced scheme-theoretic union of the labels, by the union clause of [lem-sfb-closed-component-stalk-calculus]. These are local assertions about the labelled ideals, with no irreducibility assumption on a label.

Conversely let a regular Noetherian scheme have a strict normal crossings boundary $D$, with its reduced irreducible components as labels. By [lem-sfb-snc-boundary-parameter-criterion], its ideal at every $x$ is a product of distinct parameters, with empty product off $D$. By [lem-sfb-closed-component-stalk-calculus], the components through $x$ correspond bijectively to the minimal primes of that stalk ideal, and their ideals are those primes. By [lem-sfb-transverse-prime-ideal-parameters](b), these minimal primes are exactly the distinct coordinate ideals $(t_j)$. Consequently each nonempty label occupies one distinct parameter position and their product is exactly the boundary ideal. All points satisfy the required coordinate condition, including points on no component.

source.place: Tag 0BIA (lemma-strict-normal-crossings), first paragraph of the proof and the minimal-prime identification

proof.text: For the invariance fix $y\in Y$ over $x\in X$ and affine coordinate rings $R\to T$ giving the assumed ind-etale map near them. Let $A=R_{\mathfrak p}=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $B=T_{\mathfrak q}=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$. They are Noetherian, and $A\to B$ is flat local by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability], the flatness clause in [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps]. It is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat]. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-etale-fiber-structure] the fibre ring $F=\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_R T$ is reduced and all its primes are maximal. The prime corresponding to $\mathfrak q$ is provided by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection]; it is minimal as well, since no two distinct primes of $F$ are comparable. Its localization is a field by [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-reduced-localization-field]. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-local-ring-iso] this localization is $B/\mathfrak m_AB$. Hence $\mathfrak m_AB=\mathfrak m_B$.

source.place: Tag 0AH1 (lemma-filtered-colimit-etale-noetherian-fibres), fibre calculation; the reduced zero-dimensional fibre statement suffices

proof.text: For any proper ideal $J\subset A$, faithful flatness and [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] imply $JB\ne B$. The quotient map $A/J\to B/JB$ is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-base-change] and the explicit quotient-tensor identification of [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change]. Both quotients are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian], and local. Their closed fibre is $B/\mathfrak m_AB=B/\mathfrak m_B$, a field. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula], applied also with $J=0$, one has $\dim(A/J)=\dim(B/JB)$ and $\dim A=\dim B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-regular-with-regular-fibre] and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-under-regular], $A/J$ is regular if and only if $B/JB$ is regular; a field is regular because its maximal ideal is zero and its dimension is zero [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Thus both regularity and local dimension of all the required proper quotient rings are compared, without any finite type assumption on $T$ over $R$.

source.place: Tags 07QP (lemma-dimension-etale-extension), 0AH0 (lemma-regular-etale-extension), 0AH1; their flat-local field-fibre argument applied to Noetherian quotients

proof.text: The ideal of every pulled-back labelled closed subscheme at $y$ is the extension of its ideal at $x$, by [lem-pc-closed-subscheme-base-change-ideal-image]. A label has unit ideal at $x$ if and only if its extension has unit ideal at $y$, by faithful-flat ideal contraction [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction]. If $x\in G$, choose a full regular system of parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ of $A$ realizing the active labels. Its images generate $\mathfrak m_AB=\mathfrak m_B$ by Step 8, and $\dim B=d$ by Step 9. Hence the image list is a regular system of parameters by [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. The extended boundary ideal is the product of the same distinct members. Therefore $y$ satisfies the pulled-back coordinate condition.

source.place: Tags 0AH0 (lemma-regular-etale-extension) and 0AH1, maximal-ideal generation argument; etale.tex Tag 0BIA for the equations

proof.text: Suppose conversely that the coordinate condition holds at $y$. Write the active ideals in $A$ as $L_1,\ldots,L_r$, and their extensions as $(u_1),\ldots,(u_r)$ for distinct members of a full regular system of parameters of $B$. Step 9 with $J=0$ gives that $A$ is regular and has dimension $d=\dim B$. By [lem-sfb-transverse-prime-ideal-parameters](b), each $B/L_jB$ is regular of dimension $d-1$, and $B/(\sum_jL_j)B$ is regular of dimension $d-r$. Step 9 gives the same regularity and dimensions for $A/L_j$ and $A/\sum_jL_j$. Each $L_j$ is prime, since its quotient is a regular local domain by [lem-sc-regular-local-domain]. They are pairwise distinct, since equality would give equality of the distinct upstairs coordinate ideals. Thus [lem-sfb-transverse-prime-ideal-parameters](a) applies to these primes and supplies one full system $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ of parameters of $A$ with $L_j=(t_j)$ for every active label. For $r=0$, it supplies an arbitrary full system and the empty prime family imposes no condition.

Let $K_A$ be the stalk ideal of $D$ at $x$. Upstairs the coordinate condition gives $K_AB=\prod_{j=1}^rL_jB=(\prod_{j=1}^rL_j)B$, where extension commutes with finite ideal products by their definition as finite sums of products. Contract the equality using [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] to obtain $K_A=\prod_jL_j=(t_1\cdots t_r)$. In the empty case this says $K_AB=B$, hence $K_A=A$. Together with Step 11 this proves $x\in G$. The two pointwise implications give equality of the coordinate locus on $Y$ with $g^{-1}(G)$. All arguments used stalk ideals and preserved the original labels, so no global integrality of any $C_j$ was used.
